request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The rollover now also soft-closes every period of the old fiscal year that is still open, in
start-date order, each as a soft close would (PERIOD_SOFT_CLOSED), after the ROLLOVER line.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A rollover now soft-closes every period of the old fiscal year that is still open. It goes in start-date order and writes one `PERIOD_SOFT_CLOSED` audit line per period, after the `ROLLOVER` line. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests.

**What changed:**
- **New step, `SoftCloseRolledOver.java`** (in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/period/`). After the carry step it re-reads each old-year period from the store, skips any that are already closed or soft-closed, and soft-closes the rest with the same `PeriodCloser` code a manual soft close uses. Each audit line has the same form as a manual one, with the steward who ran the rollover as `by=`.
- **`rollover.POST.yml`**: the new step now runs between `carry` and `respond`, in the same transaction.
- **No front-end change.** The rollover screen already reloads the periods when it finishes, so their new status shows up straight away.

**Two choices the request didn't settle:**
- **Permissions:** these soft closes don't check the permission matrix's "close" rule, as a manual soft close does. Only a steward can roll over, so I took the rollover itself as permission. If a sheet's matrix stops stewards from closing, the rollover will still soft-close its periods. If you'd rather it skip them in that case, it's a one-line check.
- **Undo:** undoing a rollover still only removes the new periods and the opening balances it set. It doesn't reopen the periods the rollover soft-closed.
